ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the coordinate axes label the x-axis and y-axis, and what is drawn is the graph of f'. The curve on the left starts from about x=-3 and is located above the x-axis, passes through a section of horizontal line and a downward-curving part, and intersects the x-axis at x=-1. After that, from x=-1 to x=3, the curve is located below the x-axis, and returns to the x-axis at x=3. Reasoning: The problem gives the graph of f', not the graph of f. The function f increases on intervals where f'(x)>0. From the graph it can be seen that f'(x) is positive between x=-3 and x=-1, so the interval on which f increases is from x=-3 to x=-1.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a graph of f': identify the x-axis and locate where the plotted derivative curve lies above it. The graph is above the x-axis from the left shown endpoint near x = -3 through the horizontal/curved portion until it crosses the x-axis at x = -1. After x = -1, the curve is below the x-axis until it returns to 0 at x = 3. From the text, use that this graph is f', not f. Apply the rule that f is increasing exactly where f'(x) > 0. Therefore fill the blanks with x = -3 to x = -1.
